sentences.text: 1 award in respect of the lands located in village Karala, Delhi which included the subject land, was made on 26.05.2008.

3. Since there was a general increase in the price of land acquired, the Government of NCT of Delhi issued an order dated 01.10.2008 to grant a Rehabilitation Package to people affected by land acquisition in respect of which awards had not been announced till 18.12.2007.
It is also apparent that in terms of the order dated 01.10.2008, the Rehabilitation Package was also available where awards had been made till 18.12.2007.
However, one of the conditions for availing the Rehabilitation Package was that the concerned land owners would not mount to challenge to the award already announced.
If the same was challenged, it was required to be withdrawn.
4. The petitioners had applied for the Rehabilitation Package in terms of the order dated 01.10.2008.
An interim compensation was given to petitioner no.3, but the same was not disbursed to petitioner nos.1 & 2.
The petitioners pursued respondent no.2/Land Acquisition Collector for release of the said amount and had also filed a representation cum reminder dated 13.09.2023.
Since the compensation was not released, the petitioners were constrained to file the present petition.
5. The petition was heard on 22.12.2023 and this Court had noted that the following amounts are due to the petitioners:

"(i) Petitioner No.1 (Ms Poonam): Rs.13,63,690.28 + Rs.5,07,896.73.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/02/2024 at 20:48:07 (ii) Petitioner No.2 (Ms Rajesh): Rs.13,63,690.28 + Rs.5,07,896.73.
(iii) Petitioner No.3 (Ms Sumita @ Sumita Narwal): Rs.5,07,896.73."

6. The Court had also directed that if there was no legal impediment for release of the compensation,
the same would be handed over to the petitioners.
It was since confirmed that the petitioners are entitled to the said compensation, however, the same was not disbursed for want of funds.
7. On 19.01.2024, the learned counsel appearing for the respondents had assured this Court that he would bring the demand drafts to be paid to the petitioners on the next date of hearing.

8. The learned counsel appearing for the respondents has in compliance with the said assurance,
handed over cheques of the principal compensation payable to the petitioners after deduction of TDS.
